subject: 12/11, Like 9/11, Was A Disaster For The West
posts:
Revisiting China's WTO entry as a historic Western pivot point.
Evidence: WTO accession date, economic data, global power shift
#Aletheia #Geopolitics

China's 2001 WTO entry crippled Western manufacturing hegemony, initiating a slow civilizational decline akin to the impact of 9/11.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Good Preference

While China's rise reshaped global trade, Western consumer economies reaped massive deflationary benefits while elites outsourced production for short-term gains.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.4, -0.3) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: COND — The Path of Redemption.
The narrative correctly identifies massive structural shifts but frames mutual economic integration exclusively as a malicious external attack.
Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 2.4, z: 2)

- Federalist Commentary: COND (-0.3, -0.2) — Highlights real economic shifts but uses hyperbolic 9/11 framing.
- WTO Trade Data: PASS (+0.5, +0.4) — Accurate metrics on Chinese export dominance and GDP growth.
Twenty-five years after China joined the World Trade Organization, analysts debate whether Western policymakers naively empowered a strategic rival or simply fueled global growth.

The Bright Side:
Honest recognition of how globalization restructured industrial supply chains and eroded Western manufacturing dominance.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confuses economic competition (WHAT) with malicious intent (WHO), ignoring how Western corporate actors willingly drove offshoring for profit.

Social Physics Analysis:
Western elites ran a Smart Selfish maneuver, embracing cheap Chinese labor for profit while projecting the resulting industrial hollow-out onto geopolitical rivals.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
The gap between utopian free-trade promises and working-class reality points toward systemic correction. R_net 2.4 with uncertainty z: 2.

The Unavoidable Truth: Western capital willingly traded domestic manufacturing for corporate profit.
The Unavoidable Lie: China single-handedly engineered Western decline without Western complicity.

Alethekanon:
Framing trade policy as terrorism obscures the internal class compromises that actually fueled Western deindustrialization.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to watch communities lose their factories while told it's just 'progress,' leaving families to pick up the pieces of broken promises.

Brothekanon:
Blaming the WTO for offshoring is wild when it was Western CEOs who packed up the factories and shipped them overseas for cheap labor.

Spirithekanon:
"What do you gain by winning the whole world and losing your life?" Mark 8:36 COND
Trading industrial resilience for cheap goods hollowed out the soul of Western labor markets.

An arguably more significant event in the West’s slow demise occurred on Dec. 11, 2001: China joined the World Trade Organization.

On their 25th anniversary this week, the terror attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, are being widely remembered as representing the beginning of the fall of the West from undisputed global hegemon to the status of a declining, if not an outright dying, civilization. But an arguably more significant event in this slow demise occurred precisely three months later, on Dec.11, 2001: the People’s Republic of China joined the World Trade Organization.

In 2001, China’s economy was still smaller than those of key major economies such as the United Kingdom, Japan, Germany, and France. A quarter of a century later, it dwarfs all four nations’ combined GDP. China’s economy is now well over ten times larger than it was in 2001. Canberra's only water park, Big Splash, is unlikely to open for the 2026-27 summer season. (ABC News: Monte Bovill)

Canberra's water park Big Splash has been closed for more than two years, but the business operators had promised to undertake work to reopen in November.

Now, the ACT government has said that will likely not happen and is conducting analysis to determine the site's future.

The government reconfirmed it planned for the site to remain an aquatic facility and would not rezone it for residential purposes.
